solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Having a flutter with very becoming female — it could serve one well (7)

indicators.note: V becomes F: the letter for very turns into the letter for female

blocks.note: aquiver means trembling, all of a flutter

annotation.surface: A gambler has a flutter with a very becoming woman who might serve them well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having a flutter' suggests a bet; it is AQUIVER. 'Becoming' looks like 'attractive' but is the change of V into F, and the well in the definition is a water well.
annotation.definitionFit: An aquifer is water-bearing rock that can supply a well.

entries.clue: Hostile states European supports (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so E comes after AVERS

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: Hostile nations propped up by a European ally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as countries; it is the verb, AVERS.
annotation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or hostile to something.

entries.clue: Unqualified successor to do lines for speaker (7)

indicators.note: RE lines the inside of UTTER, sitting within it

annotation.surface: An unqualified replacement is brought in to deliver lines for a speaker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' suggests lacking credentials; it means utter. 'Do' is the first note of the sol-fa scale, so its successor is RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anyone who utters words aloud is a speaker of them.

entries.clue: Female called, about to leave Calais in LeShuttle? (9)

indicators.note: CA departs from Calais, leaving LAIS

annotation.surface: A woman phones about leaving Calais on the Channel Tunnel train.
annotation.walkthrough: LeShuttle is the Channel Tunnel car train to Calais; its name mixes a French article with an English word, and the question mark flags it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Franglais is French mixed with English, as in the name LeShuttle.

entries.clue: Recovering, control steady drinking in party (11)

indicators.note: SURE takes in ANC, as a drinker takes in a drink

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
the African National Congress, a political party

annotation.surface: A recovering drinker, trying to stay in control at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recovering' reads as getting well; split as re-covering, it is insuring again. The surface sends you to rehab, not to an insurer.
annotation.definitionFit: Reinsurance is an insurer covering its own risk again with another insurer: re-covering.

entries.clue: Flower bed covering short borders can save hours (7)

indicators.note: QUILT cut short loses its last letter
QUIL borders JON, the two sitting side by side
save means except, so H is left out of JOHN

blocks.note: JOHN (a can, slang for toilet) without H (hours)

annotation.surface: A flower bed is covered to help gardeners save hours of weeding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower bed' runs together in the surface; the definition is just 'Flower'. Both 'can' and 'john' are American slang for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the jonquil is a fragrant yellow narcissus, one kind of flower.

entries.clue: US fighter plane taking time to circle round (3)

indicators.note: taking time here means taking it away, so JET loses its T
what remains goes round O

annotation.surface: An American fighter jet flying a holding circle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' pairs with 'plane' to suggest a warplane; the fighter is a soldier, GI Joe. The plane only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: GI Joe, or just Joe, is slang for an American soldier.

entries.clue: One’s bagged triangle piece — a passage from Smetana chorale (5)

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch taken from the text, here from inside the words

annotation.surface: A percussionist plays a triangle part in a passage from a Smetana chorale.
annotation.walkthrough: The triangle looks like the orchestral instrument; it is the shape of a tortilla chip, sold in bags.
annotation.definitionFit: A nacho is a triangular tortilla chip, sold in bags.

entries.clue: Make distracted husband in loveless marriage empty garage (7)

indicators.note: to be in something is to be inside it, so H sits within UNIN
love is O, so UNION loses its O
emptied, a word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: UNION without O (love, a zero score)

annotation.surface: A husband in a loveless marriage clears out the garage to take his mind off it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' reads as unhappy; it removes an O, the love score in tennis.
annotation.definitionFit: To unhinge someone is to drive them to distraction.

entries.clue: Free time put aside for book by learned person (8)

indicators.note: T is set aside to make way for B

blocks.note: a literate is an educated person

annotation.surface: A scholar sets aside some free time for a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free time' looks like one phrase; 'Free' is the definition and 'time' begins the wordplay. LITERATE can be a noun for an educated person.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: liberating a prisoner means setting them free.

entries.clue: Taxi meter running for additional minutes (5,4)

indicators.note: letters that are running are in motion, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: The cab meter keeps ticking for the extra minutes you are stuck in traffic.
annotation.walkthrough: A running meter is a natural phrase, so the anagram indicator hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: the period tacked onto a drawn match is a spell of additional minutes.

entries.clue: Partner’s corny part has endless cracks (5)

indicators.note: a word without an end has lost its final letter, so HAS becomes HA
to crack something is to break into it, so HA breaks into COB

blocks.note: the cob is the core of an ear of corn

annotation.surface: A partner's corny jokes are wearing thin and starting to crack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests stale humour; it is literal, the cob of a corn plant. The ’s stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cohab, short for cohabitee, is a partner one lives with.

entries.clue: Bound to fire unspecified number in shoot (5)

indicators.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them, so N is dismissed from SPRING

blocks.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
n is the algebraic unspecified number; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone is certain to open fire on a number of people during a shoot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; Bound alone is SPRING. 'Shoot' is a young plant shoot, not gunfire.
annotation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

entries.clue: Navy say wartime captive’s held by Polish resistance (9)

indicators.note: to be held by someone is to be in their grasp, so POW sits inside SHINE

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: A wartime prisoner is held by the Polish resistance, not the navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is polish, to shine. 'Say' flags that the navy is one example of a ship owner.
annotation.definitionFit: A navy owns ships, so it is an example of a shipowner.

entries.clue: Unclad Roman lady entertains backward people (11)

indicators.note: stripped of its clothes, the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: SIGNORA, Italian for a lady, without its outer S and A

annotation.surface: A naked Roman woman entertains some rather unsophisticated guests.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roman' suggests ancient Rome; a signora is a modern Italian lady.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ignoramus is Latin for 'we do not know', applied to people who are ignorant or backward.

entries.clue: Last cowboys perhaps protected by exercising prior agreement (14)

indicators.note: REAR RANGEMEN is wrapped inside PT

blocks.note: the rear is the last part
cowboys work the range; 'perhaps' marks them as one example

annotation.surface: The last cowboys are sheltered by a longstanding deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like 'final'; it is REAR, as in bringing up the rear.
annotation.definitionFit: A prearrangement is something agreed in advance.

entries.clue: Simple pawn forced into working years and years without any rights (4-5)

indicators.note: something forced into a space is pushed inside it, so P goes into the middle
working letters are set in motion and rearranged
R for right is removed from each YEARS

blocks.clueFragment: years and years without any rights
blocks.note: YEARS twice with both Rs (rights) taken out
P is the chess notation for a pawn

annotation.surface: A humble pawn is forced into years of labour with no rights at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds grim, yet the answer is childish slang for very easy. Each YEAS rearranges to EASY, and P sits between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Easy-peasy is informal British for very simple.

entries.clue: Prisoner behind main means of escape (4,4)

blocks.note: a lifer is serving a life sentence
aft means behind on a ship, on the main (the sea)

annotation.surface: A convict hides behind the main gate, planning a breakout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as chief; it is the sea, where 'aft' is the word for behind.
annotation.definitionFit: A life raft is how you escape a sinking ship.

entries.clue: Odd bits of ability Society considers quirky? (14)

annotation.definition: Odd bits of ability Society considers quirky?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of ability: A, I, I, Y
quirky letters behave oddly, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: Polite society judges certain talents a bit peculiar.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the odd bits of a person's ability that society thinks quirky are their idiosyncrasies.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiosyncrasies are personal quirks, odd traits that society notices.

entries.clue: Harry and Ian touring island where Notre Dame is located (7)

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are knocked about
the rearranged letters travel round I

annotation.surface: Prince Harry and a friend called Ian tour an island, sightseeing in Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: Notre Dame suggests the Paris cathedral; it is the University of Notre Dame. Harry looks like a name but is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the University of Notre Dame stands in South Bend, in this US state.

entries.clue: Peculiar pieces of ear discharge upset nurses (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reversing AXE
EXA holds OTIC as a nurse holds a baby

blocks.note: to axe an employee is to discharge them
otic means relating to the ear

annotation.surface: Nurses are upset by an odd discharge from a patient's ear.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'discharge' a fluid; it means dismissal, AXE.
annotation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or unusual objects, peculiar pieces.

entries.clue: Cover teacher facing hell in the East End (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue BED sits above ECK, facing it
Cockneys of London's East End drop their Hs, so HECK becomes ECK

blocks.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree
HECK, a mild word for hell, without its H

annotation.surface: A supply teacher faces a hellish class in a tough part of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover teacher' is British for a substitute; here 'Cover' is the definition and the teacher is a BEd, a graduate in education. The East End is working-class London.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bedeck a room with flowers is to cover it with them.

entries.clue: Tissue daughter’s stuffed into nose when cycling a mile (9)

indicators.note: stuffing fills something from inside, so D is packed into ENOS
cycled letters go round, so the last E comes to the front

blocks.note: NOSE with its last letter moved to the front
as in ten pounds a day: per day

annotation.surface: A daughter stuffs a tissue up her nose while out on a bike ride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' suggests a handkerchief; it is plant tissue. 'Cycling' suggests a bike ride; it moves a letter round.
annotation.definitionFit: Endosperm is the food-storing tissue inside a seed.

entries.clue: Weeds spread around root of brassica (5)

indicators.note: letters spread about are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Weeds are creeping around the base of the cabbages in a vegetable patch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread around' reads as weeds growing; it scrambles the letters. 'Root' is literal: a swede is the swollen root of a brassica.
annotation.definitionFit: A swede, or rutabaga, is the edible root of a brassica plant.

entries.clue: Queen bearing pens for writing (5)

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, so POSE encloses R

blocks.note: a pose is a bearing or posture

annotation.surface: A queen carries pens for writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' beside 'writing' looks like pens to write with; it is the verb, to enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: Prose is ordinary writing, as opposed to verse.

entries.clue: American with cereal chucking one bowl over (5)

indicators.note: chucking out one: I is thrown out of MAIZE

annotation.surface: An American eating cereal flings the bowl over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bowl over' reads as upsetting a cereal bowl; it means astonish.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: news that bowls you over, as a bowler flattens the stumps, astonishes you.

entries.clue: Sensual relations written about in Flaubert? (9)

indicators.note: about means turned round, so IT is written as TI
to be in something is to be inside it, so TI sits within GUSTAVE

blocks.note: Gustave Flaubert, author of Madame Bovary
IT is slang for sex, sexual relations

annotation.surface: A critic notes the sexual relations described in Flaubert's novels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sensual' next to 'relations' reads as sexy; it means of the senses. The question mark flags that Flaubert gives his first name only.
annotation.definitionFit: Gustative means relating to taste, one of the senses.

entries.clue: Egg on anorak finally wiped (3)

indicators.note: the final letter is wiped off

blocks.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive nerd, a geek; drop the K

annotation.surface: Someone wipes a spot of egg off their anorak jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as food spilt on a coat; it means urge. An anorak is a hooded jacket and also British slang for a nerd.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gee, as in gee up, is to urge a horse forward, and so to encourage.

entries.clue: Hors d’oeuvre with gin for male in swingers’ bar (7)

indicators.note: for means in exchange for, so TRAP is swapped in for M

blocks.note: meze are Greek or Turkish appetisers
a gin is a snare, a trap; it replaces M (male)

annotation.surface: Starters and gin for the men at a swingers' club bar.
annotation.walkthrough: Gin looks like the drink and the bar like a pub; the gin is a snare and the bar is the one trapeze artists swing on.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: circus acrobats swing from this bar high above the ring.

entries.clue: Scottish island wanting English sailor to commandeer ship (7)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so SKYE lacks E
to here means added on to, as in two added to three, so JACK follows SKY

blocks.note: SKYE, an island of the Inner Hebrides, without E (English)

annotation.surface: A sailor on Skye seizes a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The sailor points to a sea vessel; the ship is an airship or aircraft, hijacked in the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: To skyjack is to hijack an aircraft, commandeering the ship.
